entities.name: Anaxilas
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Anaxilas, son of Cretines, was the astute and ambitious tyrant who seized control of Rhegium around 494 BCE, subsequently extending his dominion over Zancle (renamed Messana) in 488 BCE. His strategic command of both sides of the Strait of Messina, a vital maritime choke point between Italy and Sicily, allowed him to exert considerable influence over trade and naval movements in the western Mediterranean. He established a powerful regional dynasty that challenged the rising hegemonies of Syracuse and Carthage, fundamentally shaping the political landscape of Magna Graecia in the early 5th century BCE.

Anaxilas's ascent began with his seizure of Rhegium, likely capitalizing on internal strife or external threats within the city. He then intervened in Zancle, expelling the Samians and Milesians who had settled there after their flight from Persian expansion, and repopulating the city with Messenians from his native Peloponnesian region, renaming it Messana. This dual control of the Strait of Messina was pivotal to his power. He forged a significant alliance with Terillus, tyrant of Himera, and his powerful father-in-law, Theron, tyrant of Acragas, against the formidable Gelon of Syracuse. This coalition famously led to the Battle of Himera in 480 BCE, where the combined forces of Anaxilas and his allies were decisively defeated by Gelon and Theron, a pivotal moment in Sicilian history that solidified Syracusan dominance.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Anaxilas's strategic control of the Strait of Messina made him a pivotal figure in western Mediterranean trade and politics, directly influencing the major power struggles of the early 5th century BCE and establishing a lasting regional dynasty.
